text:
Maya: Quick handoff — I'm primary for the 18:00-02:00 shift. Sam was scheduled as secondary but he mentioned he might be offline 18:30-19:15. Flagging in case pages land.
Maya: Current on-call notes: watch hosted-api p95 in us-east; most traffic is from mobile clients. Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/latency (see 'p95 spike' section).
incident-bot: PAGER ALERT: hosted-api p95 latency > 2.0s in us-east (alert_id: a-9832). Triggered at 2025-11-21T18:05:03Z. Severity: page.
Maya: I see the page. Checking dashboard.
Sam: I can try to jump on but might be AFK at 18:30 — will be reachable via ping for 15m.
Priya: I'm nearby, can take over if Sam drops. Maya do you want me as temp secondary?
Maya: Yes please Priya, assign yourself as secondary in Ops.
Ben: Noting customer impact: a subset of mobile requests are seeing retries. Tickets from 2 enterprise customers showing higher latency.
Maya: Thanks Ben — please add customer IDs to the incident doc.
Priya: Looking at traces — spike correlates with a recent routing change to new instance pool (us-east-batch-3). Opening nodes console.
deploy-bot: Deploy finished: routing-service v3.14.1 -> us-east-batch-3 at 2025-11-21T17:58:45Z (commit c3f9a2).
Priya: That lines up. I'm rolling back the routing change for batch-3 to stop sending traffic to the new pool.
Maya: Good. While rollback proceeds, p95 alerts are noisy; I'd like to suppress the p95 paging for 30m to avoid duplicate pages while we verify rollback. This is within the on-call runbook escalation guidelines (section 2.3).
Sam: If you suppress pages, make sure we keep metrics and non-pager alerts (logs/warn only).
Maya: Agreed. We're only suppressing paging on the p95 alert, not the metric itself.
Priya: Rollback initiated. I'll post progress.
Maya: Executing suppression now:```
incidentctl suppress --alert p95_latency_us_east --duration 30m --reason "rollback in progress; on-call handoff" --run_by maya
```
Maya: suppression command returned: success (suppress_id: s-7741).
incident-bot: ALERT SUPPRESSION: alert p95_latency_us_east suppressed for 30m by Maya (s-7741). Non-pager notifications continue.
Ben: noted. Customers notified via status page?
Maya: Posting status update now: "Investigating increased latency in us-east; mitigation in progress (rolling back routing). No data loss, potential degraded response times for some mobile users. Engineers are on it." -> status.redwood.ai/incident/20251121-01
Sam: I'm available on Slack if needed; if I go AFK at 18:30, Priya is cover.
Priya: Rollback completed at 18:18. Traffic diverted back to stable pool. I'm watching p95 and traces.
Maya: Great — Priya, can you check for any KV cache thrashing that might be secondary effect? Runbook step 5 mentions `redis-monitor --latency`
Priya: Doing that. Initial check shows elevated cache miss rate around the time of deploy, but it's trending down as traffic stabilizes.
Ben: Customer tickets updated. Two customers had retries but no data loss. Added mitigation notes.
Maya: Since rollback is complete and metrics are improving, I'm going to cancel suppression in 10m unless we see re-regressions.
Maya: Cancel suppression early:```
incidentctl unsuppress --id s-7741 --run_by maya
```
Maya: unsuppress success. Pages will resume if p95 exceeds threshold.
incident-bot: SUPPRESSION CANCELLED: s-7741 by Maya.
Sam: Back online — looks good from my side, p95 trending toward normal.
Priya: Confirmed. No new error spikes.
Maya: OK — closing handoff note. Action items: 1) Priya to follow up with postmortem on routing rollout validation (owner: Priya). 2) Ben to notify the two affected customers with post-incident summary. 3) Sam to update on-call schedule to mark 18:30-19:15 as covered by Priya.
Priya: Will do postmortem draft.
Ben: Will send customer notes.
Sam: Schedule updated. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
Maya: Thanks all — marking this thread resolved for now.
